description:
Instant replay export/remux pipeline for the v2 native/helper replay engine. Turns the rolling fMP4 segments captured by T-006 into a single playable MP4 with `+faststart`. Design only — no code.

Full design record: N-006. Summary in `.story/project-state.md` under "v2.0.0 instant replay export/remux pipeline (T-007)". Locked decisions below.

**Responsibility scope:** export pipeline = helper-side module on a separate Tokio task. Read-only against the rolling segment buffer (T-006). Consumes `ReplaySnapshot` (T-006 §5). Owns final-file naming, temp safety, atomic move. Calls `replay.snapshot_release(snapshot_id)` exactly once on terminal outcome. Does NOT touch capture, encoder config, or audio encode (slot reserved for future audio ticket). Electron NEVER sees frames, NEVER sees segment paths, NEVER touches ffmpeg.

**State machine:** `IDLE → QUEUED → PROBING → PLANNING → EXECUTING(COPY | REENCODE_HEAD | REENCODE_BRIDGE | REENCODE_FULL) → MUXING → VALIDATING → FINALIZING → DONE`. Any state → `CANCELLING → CANCELLED` (except VALIDATING/FINALIZING which reject cancel) or `FAILED`. Every transition emits an IPC event so the UI never has to infer state from elapsed time. Structural answer to the v1.1.x freeze-during-save bug.

**Operating modes (chosen once in PLANNING; locked at EXECUTING):**
- **`fast`** — stream-copy concat + `+faststart`. Preconditions: head trim on IDR/segment boundary, no discontinuity, all segments share codec/profile/level/timescale/dims/pixel_format/SPS/PPS. Sample timing preserved exactly.
- **`lead-reencode`** — head GOP re-encoded with **libx264 only** (Linux N-004 §13: HW for live, CPU for re-encode, no exceptions); tail stream-copied; concat into MP4. Head GOP ends with fresh IDR for clean concat. Parameters match source profile/level/colour/timebase.
- **`discontinuity`** — bridge intervals `[Pc − 1 GOP, Pc + 1 GOP]` re-encoded with libx264; outside stretches stream-copied. Escape valve: if bridges > 60 % of total, escalate to `full-reencode` BEFORE execution starts.
- **`full-reencode`** — "Maximum compatibility" toggle OR escape valve OR probe-matrix fall-through. Single libx264 pass, preset `medium`, CRF 20, GOP 2 s. Plain MP4 + `+faststart`. Linux NEVER asks HW to re-encode.

**Planning matrix (first match wins):** max-compat → `full-reencode`; discontinuity present → `discontinuity` or `full-reencode` per 60 % rule; any pairwise codec/profile/level/timescale/dims/pixel_format/SPS/PPS mismatch → `full-reencode`; mid-GOP head trim → `lead-reencode`; else → `fast`. PLANNING emits `PlanReport { mode, copy_ranges, reencode_ranges, est_output_bytes, est_duration_s, expected_fps }` carried by `export.started`.

**Cadence preservation (v1.1.0 fix as contract):** fast and lead-reencode preserve sample timing exactly via MP4 sample table — no re-stamping, no implicit CFR coercion. Discontinuity and full-reencode pass real PTS deltas through decoder→encoder; libx264 invoked with passthrough vsync. `samples_duplicated_total` MUST be 0 in production; non-zero is a defect that triggers a diagnostics dump. `fps_observed_out` computed from the muxed sample table, not parsed from ffmpeg stderr. NO fake 60 fps.

**Audio sidecar slot (future-proofing only):** mux step has `if let Some(audio) = snapshot.audio_segments { ... }`. v2.0.0 audio plan: AAC-LC, single track, shared `t0_ns` with video (v1.1.0 audio sidecar stability fix as contract). Audio is ALWAYS stream-copied even when video re-encodes; audio trim is sample-accurate via `edts/elst` edit list, not by re-encoding the head AAC frame. If `audio_segments.is_none()`, produces video-only MP4 with no behaviour change. Audio encode itself = separate ticket.

**Final naming / temp:** default output `$XDG_VIDEOS_DIR/Cove Replays/` (Linux), `%USERPROFILE%\Videos\Cove Replays\` (Windows), lazily created mode 0700. Final name `Replay-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<HHMMSS>-<duration>s.mp4` with collision `-<n>` suffix. Temp: `<output_dir>/.cove-replay-<snapshot_id>.partial.mp4` — same FS as final → atomic rename. Orphan tracking via append-only `$XDG_STATE_HOME/cove-screen-recorder/exports/manifest.jsonl` (start line before temp create, end line on terminal outcome).

**Atomic final move:** fsync temp fd → close → SHA-256 (single sequential read) → POSIX `rename(2)` / Windows `MoveFileExW(REPLACE_EXISTING | WRITE_THROUGH)` → directory fsync (Linux) or `FlushFileBuffers` on dir handle (Windows) → manifest `outcome = success` → emit `export.completed`.

**Snapshot release (exactly-once):** owned by a `SnapshotGuard(Arc<Snapshot>)` whose `Drop` releases the pin if no terminal outcome has fired. Release on success (explicit, before `export.completed`) or failure / cancel / panic / helper exit (Drop). `#[must_use]`; debug-build panic on drop-without-outcome.

**Cancel:** checked at sub-stage boundaries. COPY between segments (≤ 2 s of unfinishable work). REENCODE_* drains ffmpeg up to 5 s, then SIGKILL. MUXING discards in-progress write; temp unlinked. VALIDATING / FINALIZING reject cancel (rename race window); UI disables button. Successful cancel → temp unlinked + snapshot released + `export.cancelled` emitted. No partial-file recovery — cancel always discards.

**Queue:** single-worker FIFO. Each `replay.save(...)` pins its own snapshot immediately — user CAN keep saving while another export runs. Depth cap 8; ninth submission → `export.rejected(queue-full)` and immediately releases its snapshot. In-memory only; helper crash loses queue state but T-006 recovery offers orphaned snapshots back to the user.

**Anti-freeze invariants (structural):** (1) snapshot is paths not bytes; (2) export task does not share locks with capture / encoder; (3) every state transition emits an IPC event so the UI spinner is bound to event lifecycle not a timer; (4) per-export watchdog fires `export.stalled` at 5 s/COPY, 10 s/REENCODE_*, 2 s/MUXING+VALIDATING+FINALIZING but does NOT auto-kill; (5) ffmpeg is one-try with structured errors — NEVER a retry loop (the v1.1.x bug); (6) capture is not paused for any export stage, even full re-encode of a 10-minute snapshot.

**Failure modes (catalogue, each dumps last 30 s of counters + PlanReport to `$XDG_STATE_HOME/.../diagnostics/<export_id>.json`):** `snapshot-read-failed`, `probe-sps-pps-missing`, `ffmpeg-spawn-failed`, `ffmpeg-exited-nonzero` (carries last 8 KB stderr), `reencode-libx264-missing`, `mux-faststart-failed`, `validate-ffprobe-failed`, `validate-first-frame-decode-failed`, `finalize-rename-failed`, `finalize-disk-full`, `cancel-requested`, `helper-shutdown`.

**Helper exit mid-export:** `SnapshotGuard::Drop` releases the pin; temp file left as orphan. Next launch reads exports manifest, unlinks any temp whose start line lacks an end line, appends `outcome = orphan-cleaned`. T-006 recovery layers reclaim the underlying session and re-offer it via `replay.recoverable_sessions()`. User never sees a half-written `.mp4`.

**Diagnostics counters (1 Hz + transitions; pairs with N-003 §14 / N-004 §16 / N-005 §16):** `export_started_total`, `export_completed_total{mode}`, `export_failed_total{reason}`, `export_cancelled_total`, `export_queue_depth`, `export_queue_rejected_total`, `export_stage_duration_ms.{queued,probing,planning,copy,reencode_head,reencode_bridge,reencode_full,muxing,validating,finalizing}.{p50,p95,p99}`, `bytes_in_total`, `bytes_out_total`, `bytes_copied_total`, `bytes_reencoded_in_total`, `bytes_reencoded_out_total`, `samples_total`, `samples_copied_total`, `samples_reencoded_total`, `samples_duplicated_total` (must be 0), `samples_dropped_total` (must be 0 outside trim), `reencode_seconds_total`, `reencode_pixels_total`, `reencode_libx264_kfps.{p50,p95}`, `fps_observed_in`, `fps_observed_out`, `fps_divergence_pct` (> 5 % triggers dump), `ffmpeg_spawn_latency_ms.{p50,p95,p99}`, `ffmpeg_exit_code_last`, `final_file_move_latency_ms.{p50,p95,p99}`, `final_file_size_bytes`, `final_file_sha256_compute_latency_ms`, `temp_file_orphan_cleaned_total`, `exports_manifest_append_latency_ms.{p50,p95}`. Triangulates which layer caused any delay.

**Event surface (T-008 consumption contract):** `export.queued`, `export.started{plan: PlanReport}`, `export.progress{stage, pct, bytes_in, bytes_out, samples_processed, samples_total, eta_ms}` at ≥ 1 Hz, `export.stalled`, `export.completed{final_path, bytes, sha256, duration_s, mode, fps_observed_out}`, `export.failed{stage, reason_code, details, diagnostics_path}`, `export.cancelled{stage, partial_bytes}`, `export.rejected{reason}`. Exactly one terminal event per `export_id`.

**T-008 method surface:** `replay.save(N) → ReplaySnapshot`, `replay.export_start(snapshot, ExportOptions{output_path, max_compat, audio_mode}) → export_id`, `replay.export_cancel(export_id)`, `replay.snapshot_release(snapshot_id)`.

**Validation matrix:** fast path on all four backends × {1080p60, 1440p60, 4K60} × {12, 25, 50 Mbps}; lead trim re-encode at every preset duration verifying head GOP ends with IDR; one- and two-crossing discontinuity; 60 % escape-valve trigger; max-compat forces libx264 even when source was HW; cancel at every stage including rejection at VALIDATING / FINALIZING; helper SIGKILL recovery; jittery capture cadence preservation (target 60, actual 50, no duplicated samples); player compatibility (VLC / mpv / Chrome / WMP / QuickTime / ffprobe no-warnings); multi-save queue ordering; queue-full rejection at depth 9; near-disk-full at output dir AND state dir.

**Out of scope (deferred):** audio encode (slot reserved), HDR tone-mapping policy, AV1 export, user-facing trim-adjust UI, cloud upload, multi-track audio exports, subtitle / overlay burning, per-export bitrate override, GIF / WebM / image-sequence export. Open implementation items (non-blocking): ffmpeg subprocess vs library (default subprocess), libx264 thread count default `min(num_cores − 2, 8)`, Windows long-path support on output dir, manifest fsync per-append vs batched (default per-append).
title: Design instant replay export/remux pipeline
